source_anchor: Five Critical Lessons > 1. Liveness Probes + Sleep Loops Don't Mix
instance: gmail-tracker ran as a Deployment executing `while true; do job; sleep 12h; done`, but its liveness probe checked for /app/logs/gmail_tracker.log every 300s with failureThreshold 3; the probe failed after 15 minutes of sleep, Kubernetes sent SIGKILL, and restartPolicy:Always restarted the pod immediately, producing 850 restarts in 8 days instead of one run per 12 hours.
check: Alert when a pod's restart count/rate is anomalously high relative to its expected run cadence, not just when Status != Running.

source_anchor: Five Critical Lessons > 2. Exit Code 137 is Ambiguous
instance: Exit code 137 (SIGKILL) was treated as diagnostic on its own, but it is produced identically by OOMKiller and by liveness-probe-triggered kills; the pod was actually using only 3Mi of a 512Mi memory limit, so the exit code alone would have misdiagnosed the incident as an OOM issue.
check: On SIGKILL (137), check pod events/describe output for the kill reason ('Liveness probe failed' vs 'OOMKilled') plus actual memory usage before attributing cause.

source_anchor: Five Critical Lessons > 3. Job vs Deployment Pattern Confusion
instance: A periodic 12-hour job was implemented as a Deployment with restartPolicy:Always and an in-container sleep loop instead of a CronJob, mismatching the Kubernetes workload pattern to the actual execution model and causing the probe/restart conflict.
check: Flag manifests where a Deployment/restartPolicy:Always container's entrypoint contains a long sleep or `while true` polling loop — that shape belongs in a CronJob, not a Deployment.

source_anchor: Five Critical Lessons > 4. File-Based Liveness Probes Are Fragile
instance: The liveness probe checked for existence of a log file the app never actually wrote to disk (it logged to stdout only), so the probe was guaranteed to fail on that emptyDir-backed path regardless of application health.
check: Flag exec-based liveness probes that `test -f` a path when the container's logging config writes to stdout rather than to that path.

source_anchor: Five Critical Lessons > 5. Silent Failures Hide in Logs
instance: Pod status showed 'Running' and job logs showed successful completion on every cycle, so the restart loop was invisible unless someone specifically inspected the restart counter (850 restarts/8 days) rather than status or log content.
check: Monitor pod restart count/rate as a first-class health signal, independent of pod phase and log content.

source_anchor: What We Learned > 1. Kubernetes Network Topology Must Be Considered for API Tokens
instance: The Cloudflare API token used by cert-manager for DNS-01 challenges had an IP whitelist scoped to the homelab external network (192.168.x.x), but cert-manager's pod traffic originated from the Kubernetes overlay network (10.42.2.247); the mismatch caused Cloudflare's API gateway to silently reject the token's requests, blocking wildcard cert renewal undetected for 4+ months.
check: When IP-filtering an API token used by an in-cluster service, verify the filter includes the pod/overlay CIDR the traffic actually originates from, not just the host network.

source_anchor: What We Learned > 2. Defense in Depth Can Create False Security
instance: IP filtering was layered on top of a Cloudflare token already scoped to a single zone and DNS-edit-only permissions; the added IP restriction contributed no meaningful extra security but broke the legitimate cert-manager use case, causing the 4-month undetected renewal failure.
check: Audit IP-restricted tokens: flag cases where the IP restriction excludes the caller's actual source range despite zone/permission scoping already limiting blast radius sufficiently.

source_anchor: What We Learned > 3. Silent Failure Modes Are Dangerous
instance: The ACME Challenge object reported 'Presented: true' (the API call reached Cloudflare) even though the IP filter had rejected the request before it created the TXT record, so the only visible status looked healthy while DNS-01 validation was actually failing.
check: Do not treat Challenge status Presented:true as success; separately confirm the TXT record exists via DNS query (e.g. `nslookup _acme-challenge.<domain> 1.1.1.1`).

source_anchor: What We Learned > 4. Network Heterogeneity Requires Explicit Thinking
instance: Infrastructure spans two distinct IP ranges — homelab external (192.168.0.0/24) and Kubernetes overlay (10.42.0.0/16) — that were not explicitly documented anywhere, so an IP-based access policy was configured against the wrong range by default.

source_anchor: What We Learned > 5. Health Checks Must Validate End-to-End Behavior
instance: health-check.sh validated only pod/node status, not whether TLS certificates were actually renewing (Ready state, pending/stuck ACME challenges), so the fully stuck wildcard-cert renewal produced no health-check failure for 4+ months.
check: kubectl get certificate -A should show Ready=True for all certs; alert on stuck/pending challenges, not just pod/node liveness.

instance: Secrets were committed to the public GitHub repository because no pre-commit scanning existed to block staged files containing credential-shaped patterns (password/api_key/secret/token assignments, sk-*/ghp_*/AKIA* literals) before push.
check: git diff --staged | grep -iE 'password|api.?key|secret|token|bearer|oauth|sk-|ghp_' before every commit; block the commit if matched.
